newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, rises above ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, rises above ceiling.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar on foreign buying to test the central bank's ceiling in moderate late trading on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said offshore operators seemed to have sold dollars in large amounts to test the central bank's floor rate. The central bank did not intervene although the rate breached the ceiling, they said
But one local bank dealer said it was unlikely the ceiling of the rupiah would be touched on Thursday because of a built-in premium for longer days through the weekend.
Spot value on Thursday will be due on Tuesday because of a public holiday in the United States on Monday.
"But I don't know about next week. Offshore interest in the rupiah remains strong," the local bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,318.25/18.75 at 0920 GMT against an opening of 2,320.5/21.5.
One U.S. bank dealer said offshore players were seen trying to create ground for a band widening because they were heavily short of dollars.
Dealers in Jakarta said they did not expect a new widening for now because the central bank had widened it last month.
Bank Indonesia widened its intervention band to eight percent from five percent on September 11.
The U.S. bank dealer said some selling from London in the afternoon caused the dollar to trade slightly below the floor rate after the squaring time of Bank Indonesia at 0900 GMT.
"People who do not want to pay for the expensive swap costs on Thursday prefer to sell now and thus test the downside at a minimal cost," he said.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,318.25/19.00 and 2,318.25/18.75, respectively.
The dealer said some operators were seen trying to make gains from short dollar selling on speculation that the dollar on Tuesday would be lower.
He said offshore players had to pay for the roll-over costs but the potential gains were still high.
Dealers said short-dated swap rates remained expensive although overnight money had eased to 10.0/11.0 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.70/0.80 and tom/next at 0.78/0.80.
The local bank dealer said longer-term swap rates eased slightly as some offshore players were seen reducing long dollars positions on expensive roll-over costs.
One-month swap edged down to 18.50/19.20 from 19.25/20.0, two to 34.0/36.0 from 37.0/38.0, three to 53.5/55.5 from 55.0/57.0 and six to 103.0/104.5 from 104.5/106.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,319/2,511 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,319/2,367 on Wednesday.
